title: Stabilize tenant throughput after burst-induced eviction storm with soft-reservation smoothing and KV-cache anti-thrash
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: On 2026-02-17 a dedicated cluster serving multiple enterprise tenants experienced a throughput collapse and elevated tail latency for ~3.5 hours. Root cause analysis points to a cascade: a sudden spur of large-sequence generation requests from Tenant-A caused KV-cache churn and eviction storms which interacted poorly with our burst token policy and coarse reservation sizing. The combination caused many other tenants to lose warmed KV entries and then rehydrate simultaneously, amplifying GPU kernel overhead and triggering eviction/soft-failure loops. Impact: several paying customers saw 5-10x p95/p99 latency regressions and temporary request failures; incident escalated to on-call SRE and Customer Success alerts.
action_items: Implement tenant-level KV-cache soft-quarantine: detect >X% KV churn in 30s and temporarily reduce competing tenants' rehydrate priority for 60s
Introduce reservation hysteresis and soft-reserve smoothing: decay/increase reservations over configurable windows (default 30s) to avoid step changes when load fluctuates
Refactor burst token algorithm to apply per-tenant cooldown and cap max concurrent burst capacity per node
Add telemetry and dashboards: KV churn heatmap, per-tenant rehydrate rates, burst token consumption timeseries, and correlated eviction events
Create automated canary that replays recorded Tenant-A traffic to a staging cluster to validate anti-thrash mitigations without impacting production
Update runbook and post-incident playbook: steps to isolate a thrashing tenant, recommended reservation adjustments, and immediate mitigation commands
Ship a small hotfix to make eviction thresholds configurable per cluster (feature flag gated) so SRE can rapidly tune during incidents
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for non-offending tenants returns to baseline within 60s of a simulated Tenant-A burst in staged canary
KV-cache warm hit rate degradation capped at <=15% for co-located tenants during replayed bursts
No production incident regressions caused by the deployment for two weeks after rollout (observed via alerting and customer tickets)
Dashboards show clear lead/lag correlation between burst tokens consumed and eviction spikes for validation
Runbook updated and run through by on-call SRE with checklist sign-off
